summary: Round 2, narrow scope. R1 (false 'no module sees both halves' premise) and R2 (wrong, vacuous check-module citation) are both genuinely fixed, verified against the tree rather than against the prose: the test is at plugin/src/test/java/binjava/plugin/ThreeModesAgreeTest.java, plugin/build.gradle.kts already carries api(project(":client")) + testImplementation(project(":ingest")) + testImplementation(project(":binstore-backends")), the staged set is exactly two files with no build change and a clean working tree, and check-module.sh:337 does resolve only `runtimeClasspath compileClasspath` so the old citation was indeed vacuous. Criterion 3 now cites ADR-0023's own named check, which is the right one. R3 is fixed: bodies() projects all three ConsumerRecord components and all four SegmentRecord components against absolute literals, and the fixture separates the segment createdAtMillis (11) from the run minTimestamp (7), so both a 0L constant and a wrong-source mutation red. Nothing passed at round 1 is broken by the move: the three modes are still individually pinned (INLINE/PROXY/DIRECT via distinct inlineCap/fanOut/directEnabled fixtures), criterion 2 still observes the mode off the delivery with a never-called source, and the class adds no production code and therefore no object-store request on any path. One minor recorded below; it does not block.

findings.title: 'the grep is ZERO in both' is true of an import grep, not of the grep ADR-0023 names
findings.failure_scenario: The M5.45e cell discharges criterion 3 with "`client` and `plugin` do not IMPORT `binjava.binstore` in `src/main`, and the grep is ZERO in both". ADR-0023 § the check names the literal command `grep -rn binjava.binstore plugin/src/main client/src/main` and asserts "no matches". Run today that command prints one hit -- client/src/main/java/binjava/client/SegmentSource.java:11, a javadoc line added by M5.45g explaining why the seam exists. The rule itself holds (zero imports), and M5.45g's own cell states it precisely ("the only two `binjava.binstore` strings in `client/src` are javadoc ... not imports"), so this is a phrasing regression against a sibling cell rather than a broken invariant. The failure it invites is the next reader running ADR-0023's literal command, seeing a hit, and concluding the seam was breached -- or, worse, 'fixing' it by deleting the javadoc that explains the seam. Related and OUTSIDE this diff: ADR-0023's own parenthetical "-- no matches" became stale when M5.45g landed, which is a backlog row rather than an edit here.
